sentences.text: Muyelensaurus was a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Late Cretaceous.
This animal was more slender than other members of its group.
The fossil remains include the base of the skull, vertebrae from the neck, back, and tail, as well as many limb bones.
It is defined by unique traits such as a basioccipital condyle sharing the proximal portion of the basal tuberosity and a distal pubic ramus that is rectangular and medially curved.
A unique feature of this dinosaur is that the basal tuber of its braincase has a divergence angle of a right angle.
The genus was named in 2007 by paleontologists Jorge Calvo, Bernardo González Riga, and Juan Porfiri.
Fossils were discovered by Jorge Calvo at Loma Lindero in Rincón de los Sauces, Neuquén, Argentina.
The bones were originally assigned to the Portezuelo Formation but were later reclassified to the Plottier Formation.
Some studies place Muyelensaurus as a basal member of the Lithostrotia.
Other research places the species within the clade Rinconsauria.
A cladistic analysis placed Muyelensaurus pecheni and Rinconsaurus caudamirus in a new group within the Lithostrotia called Rinconsauria.
Muyelensaurus pecheni lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 89 million years ago, between the Turonian and Coniacian stages.
The animal lived from the Coniacian to the Santonian, between 89.8 and 83.6 million years ago.

Recent research suggests that fossil material previously attributed to Muyelensaurus pecheni may belong to sauropods from more than one taxon, potentially restricting the species to the holotype specimen only.
